recording_attribution.source_quote: Better. All of the recordings are off my test unit. None are anonymous or someone else
recording_attribution.scope: All existing Z100 Master recording batches: historical probes and scanner occurrences, separate owner scan, collision-test scan, and separate 3CH cohort. Not other models or future contributors.
recording_attribution.qualification: Same test unit does not establish the same configuration, firmware, mode, or cross-scan physical clip identity. No prototype or production status is inferred.

channel_role_corrections.reason: Owner reports a firmware labeling bug in the current firmware.
channel_role_corrections.scope: Existing owner Z100 Master card cohort only; no other models or contributors.

methodology: All successful retained video header probes are included exactly once. Filename-redacted technical samples only; original media and audit records remain private and unchanged.

Cohorts split observed channel, filename-classified mode, codec, dimensions, nominal playback FPS, and full-length versus short/partial duration. Settings are unknown; this is not evidence of one uniform configuration.
Full-length threshold: video-stream playback duration >=59.9 seconds. All other clips are short/partial. No short clip is attributed to TurboBoot or a particular startup behavior.

S-prefixed clips are kept in a separate parking-classified cohort. Filename classification does not establish configured parking mode, capture cadence, real elapsed coverage, or within-file transitions.

For this owner Z100 Master card cohort, the owner confirms the observed inside channel is physically the telephoto camera and reports a firmware labeling bug in the current firmware. The original inside label is retained as provenance; no exact firmware version or rear-camera evidence is established. This mapping does not extend to other models or contributors.

durationSeconds and rational frame rates preserve ffprobe video-stream strings. containerDurationSeconds and containerBitrate are separate whole-file metadata. videoBitrate excludes audio and container overhead. Means are unweighted per-clip video bitrate means within each cohort, not pooled camera/configuration averages.

The 19 original scanner numeric sample occurrences are retained separately without deduplication. They are not 19 additional videos, do not identify physical files, and can differ slightly from ffprobe values. App group codec summaries did not establish per-file codecs.
Firmware remains null. An owner-tentative version was not independently confirmed and is not certified here. No measured parking power, wake timing, or startup timing is established.

Bounded header inspection is not full-file decode validation, footage review, or proof of capture behavior. No raw footage, locations, original filenames, timestamps, support logs, or settings payloads are published.

A separate owner-confirmed 2CH front/telephoto time-lapse scan is retained under owner_scan. Its settings do not establish historical settings or cross-scan physical clip identity. Historical inside-to-telephoto attribution is separately owner-confirmed in channel_role_corrections. New numeric samples are deduplicated by numeric equality within channel/context; occurrence indices retain source order with filenames redacted.

limitations: Scanner labels both groups Driving/continuous; this is classifier context, not proof that every sample is driving. Front samples cannot be assigned individually to driving or parking without retained filename links. Bitrate bands do not establish modes.

The second stored folder token is anonymized; the inside-to-telephoto mapping is owner testimony, not a decoded folder token. Historical inside-to-telephoto attribution is separately owner-confirmed; cross-scan physical clip identity is not established.

Only nested retained numeric pairs are measured evidence here; 902 inventoried MP4 entries are not 902 retained probes or proof of 902 distinct valid recordings. Historical and new inventories must not be summed as distinct clips.
Codec arrays are empty. No codec attribution is borrowed from historical ffprobe probes. No container bitrate or separate container duration is supplied in these samples.
Playback frame rates do not establish capture cadence, real elapsed parking coverage, within-file transitions, power draw, or firmware. No footage was read or decoded for this update.
owner_scan.parking_filename_rule: S_ prefix identifies front parking on this owner-confirmed setup only; no per-sample filename links survived in this stored scan.
owner_scan.provenance: Separate Vortex Radar test-unit scan; cross-scan physical clip identity with the historical inspected card has not been established.

source: Vortex Radar test unit, owner card inspection

methodology: Saved successful ffprobe headers provide one canonical measurement per actual clip; video-stream and container measurements remain distinct. Header inspection is not decode validation.

AVFoundation measurements are alternate observations of the same 40 clips, linked using retained private per-sample paths and checked against size, dimensions, duration and playback FPS; never count them as 40 additional clips.

Original submitted occurrences retain all six numeric fields and multiplicity. Correspondence requires unique exact same-producer numeric equality in the reviewed channel context; native-to-ffprobe duration tolerance is 0.0011 seconds and playback-FPS tolerance is 0.04 FPS, allowing millisecond duration rounding and nominal playback-rate representation differences. No index-based array join is used.

Owner confirms main-unit front/telephoto and the configured collision-detection wake-record-sleep test. Some driving remains. All current names are ordinary, without the previously observed parking marker; every per-file driving/parking attribution and trigger remains unresolved.

Four approximately five-minute two-view recording bursts are observable in private timing evidence; they do not prove physical impacts or assign all clips to collision recording. No timestamps or file identities are published.

No bitrate change is attributed to quality, selected menus, firmware or other unreported settings. Historical and earlier owner cohorts remain separate; no cross-scan physical identity or independent-clip total is asserted.
